item.title: Chemical Substitution as a Route to Anomalous Surface Superconductivity in NiBi$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stabilizing two-dimensional superconductivity in a bulk superconducting material provides a unique route to exploring the interplay between superconducting condensates of different dimensionalities. Here, we present evidence for a distinct surface-associated superconducting state in Pb-substituted NiBi$_3$. NiBi$_{2.8}$Pb$_{0.2}$ exhibits a resistive onset at $T_{c,\mathrm{onset}}^{*}\approx8.1$~K, nearly twice the bulk superconducting transition temperature of approximately 4.1~K. The absence of a corresponding Meissner response or specific-heat anomaly at the higher-temperature transition supports its non-bulk origin. A cusp-like angular dependence of the critical field, well described by the two-dimensional Tinkham model, together with nonlinear current--voltage characteristics and signatures of a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, establishes the low-dimensional character of this superconducting state. Remarkably, the surface-associated superconductivity persists well beyond the bulk upper critical field, reaching a maximum ratio of $H_{c3}/H_{c2}\approx4.3$, far exceeding the conventional Saint-James--de Gennes value of 1.695. These results demonstrate that Pb substitution can stabilize an anomalously enhanced low-dimensional superconducting state in NiBi$_3$, providing a platform for investigating superconductivity at the boundary of a bulk superconductor.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Barik, Subhadip Chakrabarty, Achintya Low, Sudip Pal, Setti Thirupathaiah

item.title: Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2610.33808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can the correlations favoring electron crystallization also generate superconductivity in the neighboring metal? We investigate this possibility in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with repulsive Coulomb interactions. Self-consistent Hartree--Fock calculations identify a commensurate triangular Wigner-crystal state. To investigate pairing on the metallic side, we construct a crossing-symmetric particle--hole vertex using coupled parquet and Bethe--Salpeter equations, incorporating exchange vertex corrections beyond polarization-bubble screening. Near crystallization, the enhanced electronic correlations generate an effective attraction favoring chiral $f$-wave pairing. Superconductivity is confined to a narrow metallic region adjacent to the crystal, qualitatively consistent with the superconducting sleeve observed near an insulating regime in rhombohedral graphene. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.
item.dc:creator: Ke Wang

item.title: Scattering and Schmid-Bulgadaev Transition in Qubits Based on Josephson Junction Chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.33814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Josephson junction subject to an ohmic dissipative environment undergoes a zero-temperature quantum phase transition called Schmid-Bulgadaev transition form an insulating state to a superconducting state upon increasing the impedance of the environment above the resistance quantum. Superconducting qubits based on Josephson junction chains represent a system where it is possible to dynamically explore both sides of this transition by probing the scattering of individual plasma modes of the junction chain on a SQUID at the boundary which was achieved in recent experiments. Here, we provide a theoretical analysis of the scattering in the system paying special attention to the non-perturbative superconducting regime. We find that in this regime, a specific diagrammatic resummation must be performed in order to correctly account for fluctuation renormalization of the SQUID's potential. We find analytic expressions for the modes' frequency shifts and quality factors which together provide a full description of scattering. We argue that the non-perturbative nature of the superconducting phase manifests itself through a power-law dependence of the frequency shifts on the SQUID flux and through non-monotonous dependence of the quality factors on the mode frequency. Our predictions may be readily verified in modern low-temperature experiments.
item.dc:creator: Sviatoslav D. Krasin, Alexey Radkevich, Emil Rizvanov, Andrew G. Semenov

item.title: Field misalignment effect on the in-plane magnetoresistance in the high-temperature superconductor FeSe/SrTiO3
item.description: arXiv:2610.34168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The azimuthal angular dependence of the in-plane magnetoresistance provides a powerful probe for detecting rotational symmetry breaking in superconductors, which has significant implications for understanding the superconducting pairing symmetry and the intertwined orders. However, in two-dimensional or layered superconductors with strong anisotropy between in-plane and out-of-plane critical fields, measuring the in-plane magnetoresistance is particularly challenging as it is extremely sensitive to the field misalignment. Here we perform systematic electrical transport measurements on ultrathin FeSe films grown on SrTiO3 substrates. By remounting the same FeSe film to change the field misalignment, two qualitatively different angular dependences of the in-plane magnetoresistance are observed in the superconducting transition region, indicating the extreme sensitivity of the measurement to field misalignment. The observed anisotropic in-plane magnetoresistance can be well captured by our geometric model considering the field misalignment effect. Our work provides a practical framework for disentangling the misalignment effect and investigating the in-plane rotational symmetry breaking in two-dimensional or layered superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Jie Liu, Zihan Cui, Xiaorong Liu, Yanzhao Liu, Ziqiao Wang, Jian Wang, Yi Liu

item.title: Tilt-Controlled Multi-Gap Superconductivity in Type-II Weyl Semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2610.34315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In type-II Weyl semimetals, strongly tilted Weyl cones produce coexisting electron and hole pockets, a natural multi-band setting for superconductivity, yet how the tilt controls the number and relative size of the superconducting gaps remains unclear. Here we classify the symmetry-allowed on-site pairing channels of a simple time-reversal symmetric tilted Weyl-semimetal model with $D_4$ symmetry and identify the fully symmetric $A_1$ channel as the leading instability for attractive on-site interactions, supporting a fully gapped two-gap state. The tilt acts as a microscopic control parameter, redistributing the band-resolved pairing susceptibility between the two Fermi-surface sectors rather than simply rescaling the total density of states. Once the tilt sufficiently enhances the secondary channel, a robust secondary gap develops and can exceed the primary gap even at weaker effective coupling, while inter-gap coupling locks both gaps to a common critical superconducting temperature. The Weyl cone tilt thus controls the emergence and hierarchy of multi-gap superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Mingyu Lee, Myungjun Kang, Sangmo Cheon

item.title: Universal Scaling of the Little-Parks Oscillation Amplitude
item.description: arXiv:2610.34318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Little-Parks effect played a pivotal role in establishing fluxoid quantization in doubly connected superconductors and providing early evidence for electron pairing, central to BCS theory. More recently, it has emerged as an important phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order. Yet the amplitude of the Little-Parks oscillation has never been fully understood theoretically, as the conventional mean-field Ginzburg-Landau description does not account for its pronounced temperature dependence. Here, we develop a universal theoretical framework incorporating thermal fluctuations in reduced-dimensional superconducting rings. By analyzing Little-Parks measurements across multiple superconductors, we show that the resulting scaling quantitatively captures the temperature-dependent oscillation amplitudes over a broad range of materials and device geometries, resolving the long-standing discrepancy between theory and experiment.
item.dc:creator: Yuelin Shen, Zixuan Huang, Xiaoying Xu, Wei Qin, Yufan Li

item.title: Phase fluctuations dominated superconductivity in a thick Granular Boron-Doped Diamond film
item.description: arXiv:2610.34319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of a 1.2-{\mu}m-thick granular boron-doped diamond film, where tightly packed grains form a disordered network of Josephson junctions. The film exhibits a sharp superconducting transition at a critical temperature, T_c ~ 3 K. Its transport properties are well described by the Ambegaokar-Halperin theory of phase fluctuations. Direct measurements of the penetration depth using a two-coil mutual inductance technique reveal classic phase-fluctuation-dominated behavior: below T_c, the superfluid density (n_s) varies linearly over a wide temperature range - a hallmark of thermal phase fluctuations - before crossing over to a T^2 dependence at ultra-low temperatures. Both the large low-temperature penetration depth, {\lambda}(0) ~ 8.8 {\mu}m, and the slope of the linear ns variation in the thermal regime reveal a remarkably low superfluid stiffness in the range of 0.5-0.8 K. These results establish granular boron-doped diamond films as an excellent model system for investigating the role of long-wavelength phase fluctuations in three-dimensional superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Sulagna Dutta, Subhajit Chatterjee, Vivas Bagwe, Pritam Das, S. Anantha Bharathi, C. Nikhil, M. S. Ramachandra Rao, Pratap Raychaudhuri

item.title: Nodeless d-wave pairing in monolayer FeSe revealed by intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.34382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Josephson effect provides a direct phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order and has played a central role in identifying unconventional pairing symmetries1-6. Conventional Josephson interferometry, however, extracts phase information through engineered junction geometries and crystallographic orientations, rather than by resolving the internal phase structure of the pair state within a single unit cell. Here, we use a superconducting Nb tip to realize atomic-scale Josephson interferometry in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3. Despite a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum, the local Josephson response exhibits a striking intra-unit-cell pattern, with maxima centred on Fe-Fe bonds and robust nodal lines along the Fe-Se directions. We show that these nodal lines arise from destructive interference between Josephson tunnelling amplitudes associated with opposite-sign pairing components. Microscopic calculations reproduce the observed spatial pattern and identify it as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing. Our results establish intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry as a local phase-sensitive probe of pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Runxin Li, Yuchen Huo, Jiong Mei, Ming-Qiang Ren, Miaomiao Wang, Quanxing Wei, Fengyu Yao, Maowen Zheng, Qing Qu, Cui Ding, Hongtao Yuan, Zhuoyu Chen, Wei-Qiang Chen, Kun Jiang, Qi-Kun Xue, Yu-Jie Sun

item.title: Magnetic susceptibility and superfluid density of inhomogeneous superconducting films: the Tc-mosaic model
item.description: arXiv:2610.34796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whole-sample and mutual-inductance part-sample measurements of the linear magnetic susceptibility, $\chi$, of superconducting films are routinely used to obtain the London penetration depth, $\lambda(T)$, assuming uniform superconductivity. However, spatially resolved probes show that many films of current interest are inhomogeneous on micrometer scales. Here we ask whether a distribution of local transition temperatures in a fully gapped film can produce an apparent line-nodal, $T$-linear $\lambda(T)$. The film is modeled as a random Voronoi mosaic of domains with $T_c$ distributed between $T_{c,\min}$ and $T_{c,\max}$ with s-wave (also d-wave, for comparison) London response inside each domain. We show that detectable screening appears only below the percolation temperature, $T_p$, and the transition broadens with the spread of $T_c$. For s-wave domains, $\lambda(T)$ remains activated for any $T_{c,\min}>0$. Only for $T_{c,\min}=0$ does it become a power law, $\Delta\lambda\propto T^n$ with $n\approx1.7$, but then the onset of screening drops to $T_p=T_{c,\max}/2$. Weighting the $T_{c}$ distribution towards $T_c\to0$ (more low-$T_{c}$ domains) can bring $n$ closer to 1 ($n\approx1.2$), but simultaneously pushes the apparent transition, $T_p$, more than an order of magnitude below $T_{c,\max}$. For d-wave domains, the linear term survives, and its relative slope is enhanced almost fourfold for $T_{c,\min}=0$. Hence, a $T$-linear $\lambda(T)$ measured in a film with screening onset within a factor of a few of $T_{c,\max}$ by whole-sample or mutual-inductance part-sample measurements cannot originate from $T_c$ mosaicity in a fully gapped superconductor.
item.dc:creator: Ruslan Prozorov

item.title: Momentum-resolved thermodynamics and barrier-free order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors under a Zeeman field
item.description: arXiv:2610.35381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can enhance the critical Zeeman field of clean superconductors beyond the Pauli limit. We develop a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy to investigate spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric SOC. The SOC component perpendicular to the Zeeman field enhances the critical field and suppresses first-order features, whereas the parallel component favors Pauli-limited thermodynamic behavior. Applying this framework to Rashba superconductors and Ising superconductors with weak Rashba SOC, we identify the origin of the abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter at the critical field. Competing angular contributions produce a nearly flat free-energy landscape, allowing a barrier-free order-parameter collapse distinct from the conventional Pauli-limited first-order transition.
item.dc:creator: Xusheng Wang, Gaomin Tang, Lianyi He, Shuai-Hua Ji

item.title: Local Broadband Gigahertz Spectroscopy via SQUID-on-Tip DC Readout
item.description: arXiv:2610.35737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting microwave circuits are shaped by their local electromagnetic environment, yet standard microwave measurements do not resolve the local fields and device features that govern their behavior. Here, we combine microwave spectroscopy, nanoscale magnetic sensing, and topographic imaging in a single tapping-mode SQUID-on-tip microscope. The nonlinear Josephson response converts local GHz excitations into Shapiro steps, enabling quantitative measurements of microwave frequency signals and their excitation strength using only DC readout. Applied to a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator, local spectroscopy reproduces the power-dependent resonance and nonlinear bifurcation observed in microwave transmission measurements. Spatially resolved measurements map the microwave response while simultaneously recording topography and static magnetic features, including vortices and Meissner screening currents. Electromagnetic simulations reveal how coupling through the superconducting probe leads limits spatial resolution and guides localized detector designs. Together, these capabilities establish a platform for correlating microwave circuit dynamics with the local structural and magnetic environment of superconducting devices.
item.dc:creator: Senne Vervoort, Lukas Nulens, Julia Baumgarten, Daan B. Boltje, Jessalyn DeVine, Alejandro V. Silhanek, Joris Van de Vondel, Kaveh Lahabi

item.title: Growth Phase Map of {\alpha} and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
item.description: arXiv:2610.35768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $\alpha$-Ta(110), $\alpha$-Ta(111), and metastable $\beta$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2\Phi_{O_2}/\Phi_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $\alpha$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2\Phi_{O_2}/\Phi_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $\alpha$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $\beta$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $\beta$(001)/$\alpha$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.
item.dc:creator: Marius O. Eji, Tyler J. Kirkpatrick, Ty J. Cawein, Joseph P. Corbett

item.title: The fate of $s_{\pm}$ superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an $s_\pm$ superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like $d$-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full $SU(2)$ particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual $U(1)$ treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of $s_\pm$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.
item.dc:creator: Kaustubh Roy, Piers Coleman

item.title: Fermionic superfluid transition and pairing scale separation in the kagome flat band
item.description: arXiv:2610.34342v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flat-band systems provide a promising platform for exploring exotic correlated phases owing to quenched kinetic energy and enhanced interaction effects. In this work, we investigate the flat-band superfluid transition in the attractive kagome Hubbard model using large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations accelerated by fast Fourier transforms and delay updates. Through systematic calculations of the transition temperature, spin susceptibility, and density compressibility, we establish the finite-temperature phase diagram at the flat-band filling $\rho=5/3$ and find a clear linear scaling of the superfluid transition temperature with the interaction strength, $T_{\mathrm{c}}=0.0314|U|$. Our results reveal a wide separation of temperature scales between local pair formation and global phase coherence, which stabilizes a broad intermediate supercompressible bosonic fluid region of preformed pairs that bridges the normal Fermi gas and the flat-band superfluid. We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-material platforms.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Li, Yu Wang

item.title: Higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation by a superconducting antenna with vortices
item.description: arXiv:2610.35268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interaction between superconductivity and magnetism provides new routes for controlling nonlinear excitations in hybrid systems. While dc-driven Abrikosov vortices (fluxons) are known to interact with spin waves, the ability of confined, nearly harmonic vortex oscillations to generate higher-frequency spin-wave modes remains unexplored. Here, by combining time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau modeling with spectral analysis of the microwave near field, we demonstrate higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation driven by a superconducting microstrip antenna in the Shubnikov phase. Unlike conventional harmonic-generation mechanisms associated with nonlinear magnetization dynamics, the magnetic layer remains a linear receiver, whereas the superconducting antenna generates the nonlinear microwave field. We show that nearly sinusoidal vortex motion and the accompanying redistribution of superconducting screening currents produce higher harmonics that couple to spin-wave modes. This response arises from spatial-to-temporal transduction, whereby harmonic vortex motion and the associated redistribution of screening currents convert a spatially nonuniform magnetic-field profile into higher temporal harmonics. Magnetic flux quanta thus act as active nonlinear elements for frequency conversion, extending the accessible spin-wave frequency range in superconducting--magnonic hybrids.
item.dc:creator: Anton Pokusinskyi, Pawe{\l} Gruszecki, Julia Kharlan, Oleksandr Dobrovolskiy, Jaros{\l}aw W. K{\l}os

item.title: Time-reversal symmetry breaking and inherent Josephson diodes in a multi-component order parameter superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2504.19361v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking is a defining feature of unconventional superconductivity and a prerequisite of the technologically relevant superconducting diode effect. However, its realization remains rare and exclusive to proximity-engineered weak links. Here we examine an alternative pathway to spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking by examining junctions that appear in single-crystal microstructures of the unconventional superconductor Sr$_2$RuO$_4$, lacking external superconducting proximity. We interpret the Josephson coupling as superconducting domains of a multi-component order parameter based on a plethora of anomalous effects - including a field-free Josephson diode effect, fractional Shapiro steps, magnetic interference patterns deviating from the conventional flux quantum periodicity, and bias current-programmable bistable states. These microscopic devices corroborate earlier bulk probes of time-reversal symmetry breaking, giving a renewed impulse to the long-debated pairing symmetry of Sr$_2$RuO$_4$. Our results highlight superconducting domain walls as a platform for functional Josephson devices and the study of fundamental symmetry breaking.
item.dc:creator: Remko Fermin, Matthijs Rog, Guido Stam, Daan Wielens, Joost Ridderbos, Chuan Li, Yoshi Maeno, Jan Aarts, Kaveh Lahabi

item.title: Surface-induced vortex core restructuring in a spin-triplet superfluid
item.description: arXiv:2604.12682v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Observing the structure of quantized vortices can provide evidence for the pairing nature of a superfluid or superconductor and pinpoint its order parameter. Spin-triplet superfluid $^3$He supports a variety of vortices, calculated and identified so far in bulk fluid. We show numerically that the vortex core in $^3$He is strongly altered near a surface, resulting in a structure inhomogeneous along the vortex line. The effect is asymmetric with respect to the relative orientation of the core order parameter anisotropy axis and the surface normal. Coupling of spin and orbital degrees of freedom in the gradient energy of a triplet order parameter allows the surface to lift the degeneracy of two bulk vortex states connected by spontaneously broken inversion symmetry of the core. In a wide range of external conditions, the vortex structure at the surface is found to be completely different from that in bulk. As an implication, surface-limited vortex core observations in a triplet-candidate system may not reflect the bulk structure. We propose an experimental verification of the effect by measuring a transition in the vortex structure in thin slabs of superfluid $^3$He-B.
item.dc:creator: Riku Rantanen, Mikael Huppunen, Erkki Thuneberg, Vladimir Eltsov

item.title: First-Order Transitions in Weak Ising Spin-Orbit-Coupled Superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2605.03774v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ising spin-orbit coupling (ISOC) can strongly protect superconductivity against exchange-field-induced depairing, typically leading to critical fields far exceeding the Pauli limit and continuous (second-order) phase transitions. Here, using a free-energy approach, we demonstrate that first-order transitions can emerge in superconductors with weak ISOC under large exchange fields. In this regime, conventional theoretical approaches based on the gap equation fail to determine the thermodynamic critical field and instead yield only the supercooling field. Moreover, we identify two pronounced in-gap coherence peaks in the quasiparticle spectra, which represent the weak-ISOC manifestation of the previously reported mirage-gap states. Our results establish the importance of free-energy analysis in describing the first-order phase transitions in Ising superconductors and reveal distinct spectroscopic signatures of the weak-ISOC regime.
item.dc:creator: Xusheng Wang, Gaomin Tang, Shuai-hua Ji

item.title: Chirality-Resolved Spectroscopy of Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon States in Multiband FeTe$_{1-x}$Se$_{x}$ Superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2606.03637v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We employ terahertz Faraday magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe the relaxation dynamics of quantized helical Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon (CdGM) states in epitaxial FeTe$_{1-x}$Se$_x$ thin films, nodeless multiband superconductors with short coherence lengths in the moderately clean limit. By exploiting polarization-selective optical transitions, we directly resolve the helicity and band origin of vortex-core quasiparticles. We observe long-lived CdGM resonances with opposite circular polarizations for electron- and hole-like bands. This enables independent, band-resolved determination of quasiparticle lifetimes, vortex masses, coherence lengths, and upper critical fields, and reveals their systematic evolution with isovalent substitution. The results establish terahertz magneto-optics as a direct probe of helical vortex-core excitations and provide dynamical evidence for multiband CdGM states in iron-based superconductors.
item.dc:creator: T. R\~o\~om, A. Glezer Moshe, R. Nagarajan, U. Nagel, Hee Taek Yi, Seongshik Oh, G. Blumberg

item.title: Interlayer Phase Locking and Sliding Select Topological Melting Channels in Superconducting Bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2607.12401v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological transitions in coupled superconducting layers are intertwined: an elementary vortex in one layer carries both common and relative phase winding. We study a Josephson-coupled bilayer in an in-plane magnetic field using renormalization-group analysis and Monte Carlo simulations of the compact layer phases. The field drives Pokrovsky--Talapov (PT) entry of interlayer solitons, and free-energy calculations in fixed soliton sectors show PT square-root scaling over the sampled densities at finite temperature. Interlayer phase locking and sliding then select distinct Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT)-like melting channels. The locked commensurate phase melts through same-vorticity layer pairs when the geometric-mean common helicity modulus $\Upsilon_{+,g}$ reaches $T/(2\pi)$, with layer correlation exponent $\eta_l=1/4$. A stable sliding incommensurate phase melts through elementary layer vortices on a line of BKT fixed points, where $\Upsilon_{+,g}+\Upsilon_{-,g}=2T/\pi$ and $\eta_l$ is set by the ratio of the relative and common moduli. When the relative helicity modulus is identified with the relative-phase stiffness, our simulations agree with this prediction, and the common superfluid stiffness at incommensurate melting is nearly twice its value at commensurate melting. Near soliton entry, however, the dilute sliding state is unstable to opposite-vorticity layer pairs. Our results connect PT soliton entry with field-tunable BKT-like melting and identify the pair-stability condition that links them.
item.dc:creator: Yicheng Zhong, Yi Zhou

item.title: Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking in the Centrosymmetric Nonsymmorphic Superconductor RuB2
item.description: arXiv:2610.26264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Centrosymmetric nonsymmorphic AB2 (A = Ru, Os) borides exhibit anomalous superconducting properties, but the microscopic nature of their superconducting ground state remains unresolved. Here, we investigate RuB2 using zero- and transverse-field muon spin relaxation (muSR), first-principles electronic-structure calculations, and Ginzburg-Landau symmetry analysis. Zero-field muSR reveals spontaneous internal magnetic fields below Tc = 1.6 K, providing direct evidence for time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB). Transverse-field measurements establish a fully gapped superconducting state, with a gap magnitude close to the BCS weak-coupling limit. Density-functional calculations show that RuB2 is a multiband Z2 topological metal with appreciable spin-orbit coupling. Guided by the experimental observations and the symmetry of the orthorhombic crystal structure, our Ginzburg-Landau analysis suggests that an internally antisymmetric, nonunitary spin-triplet state is a promising candidate for the superconducting order parameter. This candidate is consistent with both the observed TRSB and the fully gapped superconducting state. These results establish RuB2 as a promising platform for investigating unconventional superconductivity arising from the interplay of crystal symmetry, multiband electronic structure, and spin-orbit coupling, and motivate further studies of related nonsymmorphic borides. The two muSR measurements provide complementary constraints: zero-field data probe spontaneous magnetism associated with TRSB, while transverse-field data characterize superconducting field distribution and support a full gap. The topological electronic structure and spin-orbit coupling provide context for unconventional pairing. Although these results do not uniquely determine the order parameter, they narrow candidates and highlight that nonsymmorphic symmetry may shape superconductivity in RuB2.
item.dc:creator: Ritu Gupta, Reena, Dibyendu Samanta, Jaskaran Singh, Thomas J. Hicken, Hubertus Luetkens, Jonas Krieger, Sudeep Kumar Ghosh, Yogesh Singh

item.title: Thermodynamic compatibility, holographic property and wave-function representation of generalized weakly nonlocal self-gravitating non-relativistic fluids
item.description: arXiv:2504.07296v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two pillars of physics---gravity and quantum mechanics---are usually formulated in entirely separate languages. Surprisingly, both can be expressed in the language of a fluid: a self-gravitating fluid for Newtonian gravity, and a quantum-pressure-carrying fluid for the Schr\"odinger equation. In this work we show that this resemblance can be understood within a common framework based on how the Second Law of Thermodynamics constrains the class of non-dissipative continua considered here. Using a transparent thermodynamic procedure, we derive the most general fluid model within a chosen constitutive state space involving density, velocity, energy, an internal scalar field, and their spatial gradients. The framework recovers, as special cases, the Euler equations, a restricted family of Korteweg fluids (including the hydrodynamic form of the Schr\"odinger and Gross--Pitaevskii equations), Newtonian self-gravitating fluids, and the Schr\"odinger--Newton system. We identify the conditions under which perfect fluids exhibit \emph{classical holography}: the pressure-tensor divergence can then be represented by the gradient of a scalar potential. Classical holography yields a vorticity transport law that preserves sufficiently regular, initially irrotational flows and, under additional assumptions, enables a single complex-valued Schr\"odinger-like representation. While gravitational and quantum-hydrodynamic theories were investigated separately in our previous works, the present study develops a substantially more general scalar-internal-variable construction, refines its perfect-fluid analysis, and systematically embeds the earlier models within a unified framework. The framework also identifies a thermodynamically admissible density--gravity coupling that connects classical and quantum self-gravitating fluids, although its stability, and observational consequences remain to be explored.
item.dc:creator: M\'aty\'as Sz\"ucs, P\'eter V\'an

item.title: Real-Space Interference from Quantum Metric
item.description: arXiv:2610.14048v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Real-space interference of wave packets is governed by their central momentum separation and momentum width, which set the oscillation wavelength and spatial envelope, respectively. Here, we show that in crystalline systems, quantum metric distribution in an isolated band can similarly give rise to real-space interference through the evanescent tails of a localized bound state. The location and width of a quantum metric hot spot in the momentum space set a complex wavevector as one evanescent plane wave component of a bound state. Consequently, with multiple quantum metric hot spots, the density distribution of a bound state or the total density of two spatially overlapped bound states exhibits an interference pattern, where the oscillation period and long-range decay length are determined by the momentum-space separation of the hot spots and the width of the narrowest hot spots, respectively. This quantum-geometric interference is particularly pronounced in (nearly) flat bands, where competing scales from band dispersion are suppressed. Furthermore, we demonstrate that using a Josephson STM the real-space interference can be experimentally observed through the tip-position dependence of the Josephson critical current. Our results reveal a direct correspondence between momentum-space quantum geometry and real-space interference, showing how bound-state profiles encode the momentum-resolved quantum metric.
item.dc:creator: Bo-Qing Wu, Xing-Lei Ma, Jin-Xin Hu, Jinchao Zhao, K. T. Law
